context.requirement_text: REQ-205 -- S7 scenario-harness foundation: Elixir scenario runner, business-tenant fixture seeding, and the API-vs-GUI execution split. See docs/requirements.yaml id: REQ-205 for full text (8 acceptance criteria).
per_ac_findings: AC1 (fixture port + diff-style test): fixture_shape_test.exs's moduledoc and body honestly disclose R-Co's source tree is unreachable from this sandbox -- fixtures are self-authored synthetic data, not a byte-for-byte port. No disguising found: header comments confirmed present, test asserts file count (12), per-file parse, and hardcoded load-bearing scalar fields (slug/hostname/actor_ids/name/version/graph shape). Accurate disclosure re-confirmed by direct read this session.
AC2 (Seed uses context modules directly): seed_idempotency_test.exs's first seed call per entity kind, followed by a direct Letflow.Identity/Letflow.Definitions row-count query, satisfies this.

AC3 (double-seed no-op, one test per entity kind): all four tests (tenant/user/group/definition) in seed_idempotency_test.exs use Repo.aggregate row-count assertions after seeding twice -- genuine row-count checks, not 'no error raised' inference. Conflict-branch (TOCTOU fallback) judged not independently test-triggered: reasoning re-verified as legitimate, not a shortcut -- Letflow.Identity/Letflow.Definitions are called directly with no Mox/behaviour injection seam in this codebase, and a Task.async timing race to force the actual TOCTOU window would make pass/fail outcome timing-dependent, violating this project's 'no wall-clock/unseeded-randomness dependence' rule. Code-review-level confirmation (each conflict branch read, confirmed reachable and correctly shaped) is the accepted substitute for this specific structural limitation -- same standard as other test-design gaps in this pipeline that lack an injectable seam. Accepted as-is, not required to be strengthened.

AC4 (minimal one-step api-via scenario, real HTTP, instance_state outcome): runner_test.exs's AC4 test dispatches real Plug.Test conn through Letflow.Router.call/2 and reads Instances.get_by_id/2. Independently reproduced TEST-DESIGNER's own mutation this session (see mutation_verification below) -- confirmed non-vacuous.

AC5 (via:gui recorded DEFERRED_TO_S8): runner_test.exs's AC5 test asserts step_results has length 2 (gui step present, not dropped) with outcome: :deferred_to_s8, captured: nil, detail containing 'S8' -- a real list-membership/shape assertion, not an absence check. The 'later step referencing a deferred step's produces output fails closed' case is separately, genuinely covered in runner_template_and_outcomes_test.exs ('a later step referencing a via:gui step's (nonexistent) produces output fails closed...') -- asserts api_result.outcome == :error and detail == {:unresolved_template, "produces.gui_output.wizard_id"}, confirmed non-vacuous by TEST-DESIGNER's resolve_dotted_path/2 mutation (silently re-substituting the literal template text), independently spot-checked by reading the mutation's mechanics and the test's assertions against runner.ex's real resolve_dotted_path/2 code (lines 439-446).

AC6 (moduledoc distinction): correctly judged non-executable (moduledoc content isn't ExUnit-assertable in this codebase's convention) -- confirmed by direct read of Letflow.Simulation.Runner's moduledoc, which cites both src/api/routes/simulation_test.zig and src/simulation/scenario_runner.zig by path and states this requirement does not build Letflow.Routers.SimulationTest.

AC7 (YAML dep REVIEWER sign-off): confirmed via `git diff main...feature/WF02-REQ205-20260831 -- mix.exs mix.lock` run independently this session -- only the {:yaml_elixir, "~> 2.11", only: :test} line plus yamerl/yaml_elixir mix.lock entries changed. No test needed; REVIEWER sign-off already recorded at step-02d. Correctly judged, not skipped.
AC8 (mix test / mix compile --warnings-as-errors pass): re-run independently this session (see test_evidence below); both clean.
context.audit_event_fix_verification: Read test/support/simulation/runner.ex's :audit_event clause (lines 504-530) directly: verify_outcome/2 now takes `produces` (not `_produces`) and runs resource_id/resource_type through the new resolve_optional_ref/3 (lines 550-555) before querying Audit.list_entries/1, inside a `with` that fails closed to outcome: :fail on any resolution error -- structurally identical to task_assigned/instance_state's existing pattern. Confirmed the two new tests in runner_template_and_outcomes_test.exs genuinely exercise this: 'resolves a {{produces.X}} resource_id reference and scopes the real query by it' dispatches a real POST /api/v1/instances HTTP step, captures a runtime-only instance_id via {{produces.instance.instance_id}} (not hardcoded -- a fresh UUID every run), and asserts the matched real Postgres AuditEntry.resource_id equals that captured runtime id. The paired mismatch test uses a freshly generated Ecto.UUID.generate() as resource_id and asserts :fail with matching_entry: nil even though a real row for the right event_type/resource_type exists -- proving the substitution genuinely scopes the query rather than being a no-op. Both tests reference a real, resolvable {{produces.X}} path, not a disguised hardcoded value.

context.test_isolation_check: All four simulation test files reviewed for DIRECTIVE T-4 (self-sufficiency, no shared/hardcoded state). seed_idempotency_test.exs, runner_test.exs, runner_template_and_outcomes_test.exs each call Letflow.TenantSlugFixture.unique_slug/1 in their own setup block to generate a fresh per-test tenant slug/hostname/username set, seed independently within that test's own setup, and tear down (drop schema, delete tenant/onboarding/registration rows) in their own on_exit -- no cross-test dependency, no shared mutable fixture state, each test runs correctly in isolation or in any order. async: false is used throughout (correct, since tenant provisioning needs Sandbox.mode(:auto), matching this repo's existing tenant-provisioning test convention). fixture_shape_test.exs is read-only over static fixture files and correctly uses async: true. No cross-test pollution risk found.
